### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**4** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 107d2e8497270aad611f77a81bc341f48c6d3e00` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8585084d7a39b5d3d6c54658f09fbdd338b3513d` — the merge of head `c0b712ce0b7723252c394e9e18f165773992a164` into base `107d2e8497270aad611f77a81bc341f48c6d3e00`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8585084d7a39b5d3d6c54658f09fbdd338b3513d && git checkout 8585084d7a39b5d3d6c54658f09fbdd338b3513d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 107d2e8497270aad611f77a81bc341f48c6d3e00 c0b712ce0b7723252c394e9e18f165773992a164 && git checkout -B drift-repro 107d2e8497270aad611f77a81bc341f48c6d3e00 && git merge --no-ff c0b712ce0b7723252c394e9e18f165773992a164

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 107d2e8497270aad611f77a81bc341f48c6d3e00
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

Inputs read: card #34384 body and all six comments, PR #34514 body, file list and both comments, the net diff from merge base `24b6ae55` to the head, the check-runs on the head, and the log of the one failed job.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set: no filter shape is newly refused or newly accepted. `fieldLeaves` still accepts an empty `$nin` and an empty `$in`; only the node an empty `$nin` folds to gains a field. Right.
- Answer set, native SQL strategy: `{ 'rel.field': { $nin: [] } }` on a member read through a relationship path no longer selects a detail row with no parent, in all positions `compileFilterNode` serves (query `where`, a measure's `filter`, the dataset's `filter`, the read scope and the window share the one compile). The statement changes from `(... IS NULL AND key = key) OR 1 = 1` to `(... IS NULL AND key = key) OR key = key`. Right: a narrowing, and it is the one the card names.
- Answer set, base column or SQL expression member: `joinedParentKey` returns null, so the arm falls through to `1 = 1`; the notSet leaf beside the constant has already resolved the same member, so the added `resolveFieldSql` call registers no join the statement did not carry and binds nothing. Statement unchanged. Right.
- Answer set under one `$not`: `NOT ((IS NULL AND key = key) OR key = key)` is FALSE for an existing parent and UNKNOWN for an orphan; main answered FALSE for every row. No row either way. Right.
- Answer set under two `$not`s over an empty `$nin` on a related field: main selected every row, the head selects the rows whose parent exists. A narrowing in the declared direction, stated only generally (N2 below).
- Public surface: `NormalizedFilterNode`'s `const` arm gains an optional `member`. The type is not re-exported from the package index and no file outside `service-analytics/src` names it. The three other readers of a `const` node (`filterNodeToCondition`, `renderFilterNodeSql`, `collectFilterLeaves`) and `drill-window.ts` read `kind` and `value` only, so the engine hand-off and the engine echo are unchanged. Additive and internal. Right.
- `notOf` folds a constant to a member-less opposite. Right: the fold of a member-carrying TRUE is FALSE, which selects no row, parent or not; and a lone `$nin: []` under `$not` always reaches `notOf` as the escape's `or`, never bare (filter-lowering.ts, `guardNullPolarity`, the `allowNull` arm).
- Empty `$in`: still the member-less FALSE. Right.
- Member gates: `collectFilterLeaves` still reads no member from a constant. Verified against the lowering rather than the PR body: outside `$not` every `$nin` is moved into the escape, whose first arm is a notSet leaf on the same member; inside `$not` the spec takes either the escape or a `$null: false` requirement on the same member (its own conjunct, or the enclosing one that put the field in `required`). In every shape a leaf on the member sits in the tree, so no member reaches the native join ungated. Right.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/34384-empty-nin-related-field.md` grades `@objectstack/service-analytics` `patch`, with the `!` title, the BREAKING banner, FROM and TO, and the ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. This matches what the diff publishes: a moved aggregate answer, no schema key, no export shape, no stored value. It is the level the sibling note of #33792 shipped at.
- Clause-②: `no (narrowing)` on the claim, the PR body and the changeset, and it is the true line: no `packages/spec/src/**` path is in the diff, and the diff narrows an answer. `Metadata-protocol: none` is true.
- Gate verdicts read from the failed job's log, whose later steps ran past the designed red: ADR-0087 registration passed (1 declared-breaking changeset, disposition accepted), the major guard passed (no `major`), the level axis passed (`no (narrowing)` at `patch`), protocol lockstep passed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev deviation, file surface: the root is the fold in `filter-normalizer.ts`, not `packages/spec/src/data/filter-lowering.ts`. Answered: confirmed in the tree; the lowering passes `$nin: []` through inside its escape and the normalizer is what dropped the member. The claim was amended before the edit (card comment 6931188630) and spec is untouched.
- Dev deviation, the 1,000-record cap bullet in `dashboards.mdx`: prose face, not reviewed here; it is the lane seat's to accept.
- Dev deviation, the two forced test edits: answered. Both pin the tree shape of the empty `$nin`, which now carries `member: 'stage'`; behaviour pinned by neither moved.
- Dev deviation, the dropped `--maxWorkers` flag on the first local run: no contract effect.
- `open_questions`: none in the dev report.
- SQL push-down: no finding. The fix is a predicate on a `LEFT JOIN` the statement already carries. No id materialisation and no in-app join is added.
- `Check Changeset` red on this head, claimed by design. The log shows one cause only: the foreign-changeset refusal of `scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs` on `.changeset/33792-cross-object-orphan-native.md`. Against the three conditions (pm-dispatch SKILL.md):
  1. Source-declared: stands. `scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs` states the DELIBERATE CORRECTION class is refused and left red on a pushed branch, and that the seat's record confirms it.
  2. No `merge_group` run: stands. The job lives in `.github/workflows/pr-automation.yml`, whose only trigger is `pull_request`.
  3. A PR comment naming the gate and the cause: NOT met at the time of this reading. The PR carries two comments, the docs-drift report and the review claim; neither names the gate. The PR body declares it, and a body is not a comment. This record names the gate and the cause; posted as a comment on the PR it meets the condition, posted on the card it does not, and the seat then owes a separate PR comment before the PR is queued red.
- Confirmation of the correction (landing-operations.md, the code-changing class: this same-head record judges each rewritten sentence of the one changed note, `.changeset/33792-cross-object-orphan-native.md`):
  - Sentence 1, before: "Under `$not` the native answer is the one it gave before." After: "Under one `$not` the native answer is the one it gave before. Under two, [...] the two negations now cancel and the answer is the un-negated condition's, so such a row is no longer selected there either, where it was before." Judged true. `$null` is total, so the lowering leaves it alone under both negations; the leaf compiles to `IS NULL AND key = key`, UNKNOWN for an orphan, and `NOT (NOT UNKNOWN)` is UNKNOWN. Before #34335 the inner `NOT` was FALSE and the outer TRUE. The correction is owed by #34335, not by this diff, and card item 5 asks for it.
  - Sentence 2, before: "Two native-path answers still select such a row [...]: a positive comparison under `$not` [...], and `$nin: []`, which folds to the constant TRUE [...]". After: "One native-path answer still selects such a row, unchanged by this release: under one `$not`, any condition a missing value does not satisfy, such as a comparison with a value [...] or a presence test (`$null: false`, `$exists: true`, `$ne: null`, `$empty: false`) [...]". Judged true. The `$nin: []` half is falsified by this PR and moves to the new note, pending in the same release. The widened `$not` wording is right: under `$not` such a spec takes a `$null: false` requirement, the `set` leaf is not in `NULL_SATISFIED_LEAF_OPERATORS`, so it is FALSE for an orphan and the `NOT` selects it.
  - Restoring either sentence from the base would republish a false statement. The correction is deliberate, not a filename collision.
- Check-runs on the head, at reading: `Check Changeset` failure (above). Success: Lint ESLint, Lint PM dispatch-gates, Lint scoped tooling self-tests, Type Check source gates, Live E2E UI, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected by code changes, Plan Test Core shards, Check PR Size. PENDING, and so no verdict: Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Build Core, Build Docs, Type Check workspace, Type Check consumer gates, Type Check debt ledger, Lint repo and tooling gates, Lint docs and code guards, Lint CI release and engine gates, Lint scoped query-options erasure, Lint scoped slot lookup and corpus. The new pins run in Test Core; their result is the dev's local reading until those shards conclude. This PASS is on the contract and attests no pending gate.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing, read against the published contract on `main`: `cross-object-where.ts` says "No parent, or one the caller cannot read, never matches — whatever the operator, `$ne` / `$nin` / `$null: true` included". The engine path and `/data` already answer an empty `$nin` on a related field that way. The native path was the one face that did not, and #34335 recorded it as an exception. So this diff takes no declared capability away at a consumer: it makes the spec's own refusal real on the last face, and the way back for an author (`$or` with the base relation field) is stated in the changeset.

Attempts to break it, all read in the head tree:

- A constant with a member and no leaf on that member, which would let the native compile register a join no gate saw. Not reachable: see the member-gate judgment in ①. Checked for a lone `$nin: []`, a mixed spec under `$not` (`{ $nin: [], $eq: 'x' }`, `{ $nin: [], $in: [] }`), an author-written escape, and a field already in `required`.
- A row selected at the head that main left out. Not possible: the change replaces TRUE with a value that is TRUE or UNKNOWN, and under Kleene logic that turns no FALSE row TRUE at any depth of `NOT`, `AND` or `OR`. Outside an even number of negations it can only remove orphans.
- `params` alignment and the absorbing `or`. The new arm binds nothing and returns a string, so the `or` restore of `params` and `joins` is as before.
- The mixed spec under one `$not`, `{ $not: { 'order.status': { $nin: [], $eq: 'x' } } }`. Main and head both select the orphan (`NOT (FALSE AND ...)`), which is the documented one-`$not` exception. Unmoved.
- Two hops. `joinedParentKey` returns the last hop's key, NULL when any hop reached no row; the test pins the two-hop statement and answer.
- The engine echo printing `1 = 1` where the native statement prints the key. Not reachable: the engine path carries a dotted related leaf as a `relation` node, which the echo declines.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

- N1 (nit) — the jsdoc on the `const` arm in `filter-normalizer.ts` and the comment in `collectFilterLeaves` say the member is always named by the escape's notSet leaf. Inside `$not` with a mixed spec there is no escape; the member is named by the `$null: false` requirement and the sibling leaf instead. The conclusion the comments draw holds; the stated reason is incomplete. No effect on correctness. Not on a prose face: left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up card, since a fix moves the head.
- N2 (nit) — `.changeset/34384-empty-nin-related-field.md` says "Under `$not` an empty `$nin` on a related field selected no row and still selects none", which holds for one `$not`. Under two, the answer moves from every row to the rows whose parent exists. The direction is the declared one, and the corrected #33792 note and `dashboards.mdx` state in general that two `$not`s cancel, in the same release. Fixable on the prose face by writing "Under one `$not`", or left as it is.

**Checklist**
- Shape: draft, base `main`, title carries `!`. The body opens with the attribution lines and then `Fixes #34384`, and all five card items are delivered. No other card number sits next to a closing verb.
- Declarations: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` appears in the PR body, the new changeset and the claim, with `Metadata-protocol: none`. `Skills-docs: none` is present and backed by a stated `git grep` of `skills/`. The BREAKING banner, FROM → TO and the ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` are in `.changeset/34384-…md`.
- Scope: 8 files. Source changes are `filter-normalizer.ts` (the empty `$nin`'s TRUE keeps `member`) and `native-sql-strategy.ts` (the `const` arm emits the last hop's `key = key` for such a TRUE on a joined member). The rest are three tests, two changesets and `content/docs/ui/dashboards.mdx`. No `content/docs/releases/`.
- Existing tests: two lines changed, one each in `where-equality-slot-list-refusal.test.ts` and `where-face-arms-refusal.test.ts`. Both are the empty-`$nin` tree-shape pin, which now carries `member: 'stage'`. That is a forced shape update; no behaviour either file pins moved.
- Gates: 53 check-runs on this head, all `completed`: 37 `success`, 15 `skipped`, 1 `failure`. Lint & Repo Gates `success`, TypeScript Type Check `success`, Test Core `success`, Dogfood Regression Gate `success`. The one failure is `Check Changeset`, below.

**`Check Changeset` red: by design, all three conditions stand (my own reading)**
1. Source-declared: `scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs` (`:127`, `:560`, `:572`) names the DELIBERATE CORRECTION class. It says not to restore the note, to declare the correction on the PR, and that the dispatching seat confirms it by its own record.
2. No `merge_group` run: the job is in `.github/workflows/pr-automation.yml`, whose only trigger is `pull_request`.
3. A PR comment names the gate and the cause: L2 record 6932908866 and final-head comment 6934382705, both on this PR. The body declares the correction too (line "DELIBERATE CORRECTION of the unreleased `.changeset/33792-…md`").
- Confirmation of the correction, by this record: `.changeset/33792-cross-object-orphan-native.md` is still pending on `main`, so it is unreleased. Its two rewritten sentences are true at this head:
  - Its old `$nin: []` exception is exactly what this diff removes; the moved half now lives in the new note in the same release.
  - The double-`$not` sentence describes #34335's behaviour, which card item 5 asks to state. Restoring either sentence from the base would republish a false statement.

**Prose faces, sentence by sentence (`dashboards.mdx`; the changeset sentences are covered by L2 ② and checked again here)**
- Path table, engine row "Up to three relationships (ADR-0071's hop limit), each read as the caller": true. `CROSS_OBJECT_WHERE_MAX_HOPS = 3` (`cross-object-where.ts:95`), and `objectql-strategy.ts:277` refuses past it.
- Refusal bullet "a path of four or more relationships (`line.plan.order.customer.tier`)": true. The refusal fires on `segments.length - 1 > 3` (`cross-object-where.ts:206`), and the example has four hops.
- "`$nin: []` (an empty list, which excludes no value) selects every row whose related record exists": true at this head. The native compile now emits `"ALIAS"."id" = "ALIAS"."id"` in place of `1 = 1` for a joined member; the engine path already matched.
- "One native-path exception remains, under `$not` … one a missing value does not satisfy, such as a comparison with a value … or a presence test (`$null: false`, `$exists: true`, `$ne: null`, `$empty: false`)": true, per L2 ② (a `set` leaf is not in `NULL_SATISFIED_LEAF_OPERATORS`).
- "Two `$not`s cancel": true, per L2 ② (`NOT (NOT UNKNOWN)` is UNKNOWN for an orphan).
- "A related field in a dataset's own `filter` is evaluated on both paths … a measure's own `filter` is still evaluated only on the native SQL path": true. `objectql-strategy.ts:597` and `:1294` serve the dataset filter's cross-object leaves (#33626), and the measure filter refusal is unchanged.
- The 1,000-record bullet: the second sentence (ids read first for another datasource, a federated object, or a driver with no subquery, cap 1000, `400 INVALID_FILTER`, never truncated) matches `content/docs/protocol/objectql/query-syntax.mdx:705-720`. **Deviation D1, accepted:** the opening clause "On a SQL datasource the related condition runs inside the same statement, as a subquery, so the number … is not limited" is broader than `query-syntax.mdx:715-725`. There, a related object on a SQL datasource still keeps the id read and its cap when an object-scoped middleware or `afterFind` hook shapes its reads, or when it is read under different driver options (its tenant scope). The bullet points to that list ("the full list is in Query Syntax"), so a reader is not left with a wrong rule, but the opening clause should say "usually" or name those cases. Not REWORK: moving the head for one clause would re-open L2 and CI. It goes on the same follow-up card as L2's N1/N2.

**Spot checks (mine)**
1. On a base column or an expression, `joinedParentKey` returns nothing, so the constant is still `1 = 1` and the statement is byte-identical to `main` (the body's claim). The empty `$in` is still the member-less FALSE.
2. `resolveFieldSql` is called in the new `const` arm only for its side effect: it registers the path's joins before `joinedParentKey` reads them, the same order the leaf arm uses. It binds nothing, so no parameter index shifts.
3. Under one `$not`, the escape `(notSet AND key=key) OR key=key` is UNKNOWN for an orphan and TRUE for an existing parent, so `NOT` selects neither. That matches the new changeset's "Under `$not` … still selects none" for one negation. See N2 below for two.

**Accepted deviations, owed as ONE follow-up card after landing**: L2's N1 (the jsdoc reason in `filter-normalizer.ts` / `collectFilterLeaves` is incomplete inside `$not` with a mixed spec), L2's N2 (the new changeset's "Under `$not`" holds for one negation; the same release's corrected #33792 note and `dashboards.mdx` state that two cancel), and D1 above.

**L2 owed: yes, and on record.** It is owed at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` because of the `(narrowing)` declaration. The record is PASS 6932908866 at this same head (claim 6932800650), with no must-fix and no should-fix.
